  power_override: null   # leave null to use the prespecified rule; set e.g. 7 for a sensitivity run

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

# 1. Aim

Run WGCNA on the strand-corrected top-5000 VST matrix and relate the modules to TILs
High vs Low instead of the three NMF clusters used before.

* Low TILs  = TILs < 10 (this includes the text value "<5")
* High TILs = TILs >= 10
* The trait is coded High = 1, Low = 0. Positive module correlation = higher in High TILs.
* The cutoff of 10 is fixed in advance (group sizes at 10%: 16 Low and 14 High among the
  30 samples that have a TILs value). Other cutoffs would only be sensitivity analyses.
* One sample (TP17-M11) has a blank TILs value. It stays in the network but is left out
  of the TILs correlations and tests.

# 2. Settings

```{r settings}
SEED <- 42
set.seed(SEED)

TIL_CUTOFF <- 10                        # High >= cutoff, Low < cutoff

# ---- paths (edit here only) ----
root <- "/ix1/alee/LO_LAB/Personal/Rahul/pILC/RNASeq"
clinical_path <- file.path(root, "Clinical_correlation",
                           "pILC_ClinicoPathological_details.csv")
expr_path <- file.path(root, "4_Count_file_HTSeq_stranded", "VST_data_GENCODEv47",
                       "htseq_VST_gene_names_top5000_variable_genes.csv")
oncovar_file <- "/ix1/alee/LO_LAB/Personal/Rahul/BioNano/Reference/TCGA.BRCA.all.genes.OncoVar.tsv"

# wgcna_base: power-independent diagnostics. wgcna_dir (power_<N>) is set once the power is chosen.
wgcna_base <- file.path(root, "WGCNA", "TILs", "High_vs_Low_10pct")
dir.create(wgcna_base, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

POWERS           <- c(1:10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20)  # candidate soft-threshold powers
R2_CUTOFF        <- 0.80                          # scale-free fit threshold
NETWORK_TYPE     <- "unsigned"                    # same as the cluster run
DEEP_SPLIT       <- 2                             # dynamic tree cut sensitivity
MIN_MODULE_SIZE  <- 30                            # smallest allowed module
MERGE_CUT_HEIGHT <- 0.25                          # merge modules with eigengene r > 0.75
HUB_FDR_CUTOFF   <- 0.05                          # BH-FDR (High vs Low test) for hub genes
HUB_KME_CUTOFF   <- 0.70                          # module membership for hub genes
TOP_N            <- 50                            # genes per module in top-hub tables

GROUP_COLORS <- c(Low = "#9ecae1", High = "#08519c")

stopifnot(file.exists(clinical_path), file.exists(expr_path))

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(WGCNA)
  library(dplyr)

try(WGCNA::allowWGCNAThreads(), silent = TRUE)
```

# 3. Helper functions

```{r helpers}
# Make IDs comparable: trim spaces, dots -> hyphens, drop a trailing _S<number>
norm_id <- function(x) sub("_S[0-9]+$", "", gsub("\\.", "-", trimws(x)))

# Save the same plot as PNG and PDF, then show it in the report.
# out_dir defaults to the power-specific folder (wgcna_dir, defined once the power is chosen);
# power-independent figures pass out_dir = wgcna_base explicitly.
save_fig <- function(name, plot_fun, width_in, height_in, res = 200, out_dir = wgcna_dir) {
  png(file.path(out_dir, paste0(name, ".png")),
      width = width_in * res, height = height_in * res, res = res)
  tryCatch(plot_fun(), finally = dev.off())
  pdf(file.path(out_dir, paste0(name, ".pdf")),
      width = width_in, height = height_in)
  tryCatch(plot_fun(), finally = dev.off())
  plot_fun()
}

# Parse the TILs column. Returns the raw text, a numeric value for plotting and
# rank tests, and the Low/High group.
#   "<5"  -> Low. Numeric value 2.5 (midpoint) is used for plotting only;
#            rank-based tests are not affected by the exact value as long as it is < 5.
#   "10"  -> numeric 10, High (>= cutoff)
#   anything unreadable (or "<x" with x > cutoff, which is ambiguous) -> NA
parse_tils <- function(x, cutoff) {
  raw    <- trimws(as.character(x))
  is_lt  <- grepl("^<", raw)
  num    <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(gsub("[^0-9.]", "", raw)))
  num[is.na(raw) | raw == ""] <- NA

  plot_value <- ifelse(is_lt, num / 2, num)
  group <- ifelse(is_lt & !is.na(num) & num <= cutoff, "Low",
           ifelse(!is_lt & !is.na(num) & num >= cutoff, "High",
           ifelse(!is_lt & !is.na(num) & num <  cutoff, "Low", NA)))
  group[grepl("^>", raw)] <- NA     # a ">x" value is not expected; treat as unreadable
  data.frame(TILs_raw = raw, TILs_value = plot_value, TILs_less_than = is_lt,
             TILs_group = group, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}

# Row-z-scored heatmap of the given genes, samples ordered by TILs group (Low, then High).
make_tils_heatmap <- function(genes, expr, traits, column_title, row_title = NULL) {
  ord <- rownames(traits)[order(traits$TILs_group)]
  m <- t(as.matrix(expr[ord, genes, drop = FALSE]))       # genes x samples
  v <- apply(m, 1, var, na.rm = TRUE)
  m <- m[!is.na(v) & v > 0, , drop = FALSE]               # drop zero-variance genes
  if (nrow(m) < 2) return(NULL)                           # need >= 2 genes
  z <- t(scale(t(m)))
  ann <- HeatmapAnnotation(
    TILs = as.character(traits[ord, "TILs_group"]),
    col = list(TILs = GROUP_COLORS),
    na_col = "grey80"
  )
  Heatmap(z, name = "Z-score", top_annotation = ann,
          cluster_rows = TRUE, cluster_columns = FALSE,
          show_column_names = FALSE,
          row_names_gp = grid::gpar(fontsize = 6),
          column_title = column_title, row_title = row_title)
}
```

# 4. WGCNA with TILs High vs Low as the external trait

WGCNA groups genes that rise and fall together across samples into modules. Here the
modules are related to one external trait: TILs High (1) vs Low (0), with the cutoff set
in the settings (10%). The workflow is the same as the earlier WGCNA with the three NMF
clusters; only the external trait is different (two TILs groups instead of three clusters).

Important: the network and the modules are built from the expression data alone and do
not use any trait. With the same VST matrix and the same settings, the modules are
therefore expected to be the same as in the cluster WGCNA. A check against the saved
cluster result is printed below. What changes is the trait part: which modules relate to
TILs, and which genes are hub genes.

Notes for future reference:

* Modules are defined before, and independently of, any external trait. If the check in
  the section "Check: are the modules the same as in the cluster WGCNA?" prints TRUE,
  the modules used here ARE the cluster WGCNA modules (same colours, same genes). Only
  the trait step (which modules relate to TILs, which genes are hub genes) is new.
* Every module-trait correlation uses all samples that have the trait. What matters for
  power is the size of the smaller group. A one-vs-rest cluster trait splits the samples
  about 10 vs 21. The TILs trait splits the 30 samples with a TILs value into 16 Low and
  14 High at the 10% cutoff, so its smaller group is larger than a cluster.

* Trait coding: High = 1, Low = 0. A positive correlation means the module is higher in
  High-TILs tumours, a negative one means it is higher in Low-TILs tumours. A separate
  "Low" trait would be the exact mirror image (same |r|, opposite sign), so it is not added.
* As a supporting view, the continuous TILs value (Spearman) is reported per module too.
* Power rule (prespecified): the lowest tested power with signed scale-free R-squared >= 0.80,
  while checking that mean connectivity has not collapsed.
* Outputs that do not depend on the power go to `wgcna_base`; everything else goes to
  its own `power_<N>` folder.

# 5. Load VST-transformed expression data

The VST matrix is already variance-stabilised and restricted to the 5000 most variable
genes, which keeps the network computation light and is the usual WGCNA practice.

```{r load-vst}
expr_data <- read.csv(expr_path, header = TRUE, check.names = FALSE)

stopifnot("Expected a 'Gene' column" = "Gene" %in% colnames(expr_data))
stopifnot("Duplicate gene symbols in the VST file" = !anyDuplicated(expr_data$Gene))

cat("Genes x columns in file:", nrow(expr_data), "x", ncol(expr_data), "\n")
expr_data[1:3, 1:5]
```

# 6. Convert to WGCNA format (rows = samples, columns = genes)

```{r prepare-dat-expr}
expr_matrix <- expr_data |>
  column_to_rownames(var = "Gene") |>
  as.matrix()

storage.mode(expr_matrix) <- "numeric"
stopifnot("Non-numeric or missing values in the VST matrix" = !anyNA(expr_matrix))

dat_expr <- as.data.frame(t(expr_matrix), check.names = FALSE)
rownames(dat_expr) <- norm_id(rownames(dat_expr))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(rownames(dat_expr)))

cat("WGCNA expression matrix:", nrow(dat_expr), "samples x", ncol(dat_expr), "genes\n")
```

# 7. Identify problematic genes and samples

`goodSamplesGenes()` flags genes/samples with too many missing values or zero variance.

```{r good-samples-genes}
gsg <- goodSamplesGenes(dat_expr, verbose = 3)
gsg$allOK

if (!gsg$allOK) {
  if (sum(!gsg$goodGenes) > 0) {
    cat("Removing genes:\n"); print(colnames(dat_expr)[!gsg$goodGenes])
  }
  if (sum(!gsg$goodSamples) > 0) {
    cat("Removing samples:\n"); print(rownames(dat_expr)[!gsg$goodSamples])
  }
  dat_expr <- dat_expr[gsg$goodSamples, gsg$goodGenes, drop = FALSE]
}

cat("Final matrix:", nrow(dat_expr), "samples x", ncol(dat_expr), "genes\n")
```

# 8. Sample clustering to look for outliers

```{r sample-clustering}
sampleTree <- hclust(dist(dat_expr), method = "average")

plot_sample_tree <- function() {
  op <- par(cex = 0.6, mar = c(0, 4, 2, 0))
  on.exit(par(op))
  plot(sampleTree, main = "Sample clustering to detect outliers",
       sub = "", xlab = "", cex.lab = 1.5, cex.axis = 1.5, cex.main = 2)
}

save_fig("sample_clustering_outliers", plot_sample_tree, width_in = 8, height_in = 5.5,
         out_dir = wgcna_base)

# No sample is removed automatically based on the dendrogram alone.
# If a true outlier is found, document the cutoff and the exclusion explicitly.
```

# 9. Soft-threshold power analysis

WGCNA raises correlations to a power so that strong correlations are kept and weak ones
are suppressed, giving a network that is approximately scale-free (a few highly
connected genes, many weakly connected ones).

```{r pick-soft-threshold}
spt <- pickSoftThreshold(
  dat_expr,
  powerVector = POWERS,
  networkType = NETWORK_TYPE,
  verbose = 5
)

sft_table <- spt$fitIndices
stopifnot(all(c("Power", "SFT.R.sq", "mean.k.") %in% colnames(sft_table)))

sft_table

write.csv(sft_table, file.path(wgcna_base, "SoftThreshold_Diagnostics.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

# 10. Plot scale-free topology fit

The dashed line marks the R-squared cutoff.

```{r scale-independence}
plot_scale_independence <- function() {
  op <- par(mar = c(5, 5, 2, 2))
  on.exit(par(op))
  plot(sft_table$Power, sft_table$SFT.R.sq, type = "n",
       xlab = "Soft threshold (power)",
       ylab = expression("Scale-free topology model fit (signed " * R^2 * ")"),
       main = "Scale independence")
  text(sft_table$Power, sft_table$SFT.R.sq, labels = sft_table$Power, col = "red")
  abline(h = R2_CUTOFF, col = "red", lty = 2)
}

save_fig("scale_independence", plot_scale_independence, width_in = 6.5, height_in = 5.5,
         out_dir = wgcna_base)
```

# 11. Plot mean connectivity

A good power gives acceptable scale-free fit without destroying connectivity.

```{r mean-connectivity}
plot_mean_connectivity <- function() {
  op <- par(mar = c(5, 5, 2, 2))
  on.exit(par(op))
  plot(sft_table$Power, sft_table[["mean.k."]], type = "n",
       xlab = "Soft threshold (power)", ylab = "Mean connectivity",
       main = "Mean connectivity")
  text(sft_table$Power, sft_table[["mean.k."]], labels = sft_table$Power, col = "red")
}

save_fig("mean_connectivity", plot_mean_connectivity, width_in = 6.5, height_in = 5.5,
         out_dir = wgcna_base)
```

# 12. Select the soft-threshold power with the prespecified rule

By default the power is taken from the data: the lowest tested power with R-squared >= 0.80.
Nothing is hard-coded. Please inspect the mean-connectivity plot at the selected power.

For a sensitivity analysis, `power_override` (see the header) can force another tested
power. The run summary then records that the power was set manually and also records
the power that the rule would have chosen, so the two cases cannot be confused.

```{r select-soft-power}
power_summary <- data.frame(
  Power = sft_table$Power,
  SFT_R2 = sft_table$SFT.R.sq,
  MeanConnectivity = sft_table[["mean.k."]]
)

power_candidates <- power_summary |>
  filter(is.finite(SFT_R2), SFT_R2 >= R2_CUTOFF) |>
  arrange(Power)

write.csv(power_candidates,
          file.path(wgcna_base, "SoftThreshold_Candidate_Powers_R2ge0.80.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)

cat("Powers meeting SFT R-squared >=", R2_CUTOFF, ":\n")
print(power_candidates)

# Power chosen by the prespecified rule (NA if no tested power qualifies).
rule_power <- if (nrow(power_candidates) > 0) min(power_candidates$Power) else NA_real_

if (!is.null(params$power_override)) {
  # Sensitivity analysis: the power is forced, and this is recorded in the run summary.
  stopifnot("power_override must be one of the tested POWERS" = params$power_override %in% POWERS)
  softPower <- params$power_override
  power_source <- "Manual override (sensitivity analysis)"
  warning("Using manual power ", softPower, "; the prespecified rule gives ", rule_power, ".")
} else {
  if (is.na(rule_power)) {
    stop(
      "No tested power reached SFT R-squared >= ", R2_CUTOFF, ". ",
      "Inspect scale_independence.png and the WGCNA FAQ guidance on powers for small ",
      "sample sizes before choosing a power by hand; do not force a historical value."
    )
  }
  softPower <- rule_power   # objective rule: lowest qualifying power
  power_source <- "Prespecified rule (lowest power with SFT R-squared >= 0.80)"
}

# Everything that depends on the power goes into its own subfolder.
wgcna_dir <- file.path(wgcna_base, paste0("power_", softPower))
dir.create(wgcna_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
cat("Outputs that depend on the power are written to:", wgcna_dir, "\n")

selected_power_summary <- power_summary |> filter(Power == softPower)
cat("\nSelected soft-threshold power =", softPower, "\n")
print(selected_power_summary)

write.csv(selected_power_summary,
          file.path(wgcna_dir, "Selected_SoftThreshold_Power.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)
```

# 13. Adjacency matrix and Topological Overlap Matrix (TOM)

The adjacency is the gene-gene correlation raised to the selected power. The TOM
measures shared neighbours, which makes modules more robust to noise.

```{r adjacency-tom}
adjacency_matrix <- adjacency(dat_expr, power = softPower, type = NETWORK_TYPE)
TOM <- TOMsimilarity(adjacency_matrix, TOMType = NETWORK_TYPE)
TOM.dissimilarity <- 1 - TOM

rm(adjacency_matrix, TOM)   # free memory
invisible(gc())
```

# 14. Gene clustering and dynamic module detection

```{r module-construction}
geneTree <- hclust(as.dist(TOM.dissimilarity), method = "average")

Modules <- cutreeDynamic(
  dendro = geneTree,
  distM = TOM.dissimilarity,
  deepSplit = DEEP_SPLIT,
  pamRespectsDendro = FALSE,
  minClusterSize = MIN_MODULE_SIZE
)

table(Modules)                      # label 0 = genes not assigned to any module
ModuleColors <- labels2colors(Modules)   # label 0 becomes "grey"
table(ModuleColors)
```

# 15. Module eigengenes

An eigengene is the first principal component of a module: one expression profile that
summarises the whole module across samples.

```{r module-eigengenes}
MElist <- moduleEigengenes(dat_expr, colors = ModuleColors)
MEs_initial <- MElist$eigengenes
rownames(MEs_initial) <- rownames(dat_expr)   # rows follow dat_expr by construction

write.csv(MEs_initial,
          file.path(wgcna_dir, "ModuleEigengenes_BeforeMerging.csv"),
          row.names = TRUE)
```

# 16. Merge highly similar modules

Modules whose eigengenes correlate above 0.75 (dissimilarity < 0.25) are merged.

```{r module-merging}
ME.dissimilarity <- 1 - cor(MElist$eigengenes, use = "complete")
METree <- hclust(as.dist(ME.dissimilarity), method = "average")

plot_me_tree <- function() {
  op <- par(mar = c(0, 4, 2, 0), cex = 0.6)
  on.exit(par(op))
  plot(METree, main = "Clustering of module eigengenes", xlab = "", sub = "")
  abline(h = MERGE_CUT_HEIGHT, col = "red")
}
save_fig("module_eigengene_clustering", plot_me_tree, width_in = 8, height_in = 5.5)

merge <- mergeCloseModules(dat_expr, ModuleColors, cutHeight = MERGE_CUT_HEIGHT, verbose = 3)

mergedColors <- merge$colors
mergedMEs <- merge$newMEs
rownames(mergedMEs) <- rownames(dat_expr)     # rows follow dat_expr by construction

names(ModuleColors) <- colnames(dat_expr)
names(mergedColors) <- colnames(dat_expr)
stopifnot(identical(names(mergedColors), colnames(dat_expr)))

plot_gene_dendro <- function() {
  plotDendroAndColors(
    dendro = geneTree,
    colors = cbind(ModuleColors, mergedColors),
    groupLabels = c("Original Module", "Merged Module"),
    dendroLabels = FALSE, hang = 0.03, addGuide = TRUE, guideHang = 0.05,
    main = "Gene dendrogram and module colors: original and merged"
  )
}
save_fig("Module_Dendrogram_with_Colors", plot_gene_dendro, width_in = 10, height_in = 7)

cat("Modules before merging:", length(unique(ModuleColors)), "\n")
cat("Modules after merging :", length(unique(mergedColors)), "\n")
print(sort(table(ModuleColors), decreasing = TRUE))
print(sort(table(mergedColors), decreasing = TRUE))

write.csv(
  data.frame(Gene = colnames(dat_expr),
             OriginalModule = unname(ModuleColors),
             MergedModule = unname(mergedColors)),
  file.path(wgcna_dir, "Gene_Module_Assignments.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

# 17. Load and align the TILs traits

TILs are read from the clinical table and matched to the expression samples. The network
uses all samples in the expression matrix; a sample whose TILs value is blank would
simply have a missing trait value and is left out of the TILs correlations only.

```{r tils-traits}
clin <- read.csv(clinical_path, check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
stopifnot("Sample" %in% colnames(clin), "TILs (%)" %in% colnames(clin))
clin$id <- norm_id(clin$Sample)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(clin$id))

tils <- parse_tils(clin[["TILs (%)"]], TIL_CUTOFF)
clin_tils <- data.frame(id = clin$id, TILs_input = clin[["TILs (%)"]], tils,
                        stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Every expression sample must be found in the clinical table (an ID mismatch would
# otherwise look like missing TILs).
not_in_clin <- setdiff(rownames(dat_expr), clin_tils$id)
if (length(not_in_clin) > 0) {
  print(not_in_clin)
  stop("Expression samples not found in the clinical table (check the sample IDs).")
}

m_t <- match(rownames(dat_expr), clin_tils$id)
datTraits <- data.frame(
  TILs_group = factor(clin_tils$TILs_group[m_t], levels = c("Low", "High")),
  TILs_value = clin_tils$TILs_value[m_t],
  row.names  = rownames(dat_expr)
)
stopifnot(identical(rownames(dat_expr), rownames(datTraits)))

no_tils <- rownames(datTraits)[is.na(datTraits$TILs_group)]
cat("Samples without a usable TILs group:", length(no_tils),
    if (length(no_tils) > 0) paste0("(", paste(no_tils, collapse = ", "), ")"), "\n")
cat("TILs group sizes (Low = <", TIL_CUTOFF, ", High = >=", TIL_CUTOFF, "):\n", sep = "")
print(table(datTraits$TILs_group, useNA = "ifany"))
print(table(clin_tils$TILs_input[m_t], useNA = "ifany"))

```

# 18. Numeric TILs trait

```{r numeric-tils-trait}
datTraitsNum <- matrix(as.numeric(datTraits$TILs_group == "High"), ncol = 1,
                       dimnames = list(rownames(datTraits), "TILs_High"))
stopifnot(identical(rownames(dat_expr), rownames(datTraitsNum)))

write.csv(data.frame(Sample = rownames(datTraits),
                     TILs_input = clin_tils$TILs_input[m_t], datTraits,
                     TILs_High = datTraitsNum[, "TILs_High"]),
          file.path(wgcna_dir, "TILs_Trait_Matrix.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

# 19. Check: are the modules the same as in the cluster WGCNA?

```{r check-vs-cluster-run}
cluster_rds <- file.path(root, "WGCNA", "NMFcluster", "K3_50runs",
                         paste0("power_", softPower), "WGCNA_Cluster_Core_Objects.rds")
if (file.exists(cluster_rds)) {
  old <- readRDS(cluster_rds)
  same <- identical(names(old$mergedColors), names(mergedColors)) &&
          identical(unname(old$mergedColors), unname(mergedColors))
  cat("Module assignment identical to the cluster WGCNA run (power", softPower, "):", same, "\n")
} else {
  cat("Cluster WGCNA result for power", softPower, "not found; check skipped.\n")
}
```

# 20. Module-TILs associations

```{r module-tils-associations}
MEs <- orderMEs(mergedMEs)
stopifnot(identical(rownames(dat_expr), rownames(MEs)))
write.csv(MEs, file.path(wgcna_dir, "ModuleEigengenes_Merged.csv"), row.names = TRUE)

nGenes   <- ncol(dat_expr)
nSamples <- nrow(dat_expr)
ok       <- !is.na(datTraitsNum[, "TILs_High"])
n_trait  <- sum(ok)
cat("Samples in network:", nSamples, "| with a TILs group:", n_trait,
    "| High:", sum(datTraitsNum[ok, "TILs_High"] == 1),
    "| Low:", sum(datTraitsNum[ok, "TILs_High"] == 0), "\n")

# Pearson correlation of each module eigengene with the 0/1 trait (High = 1)
module.trait.correlation <- cor(MEs, datTraitsNum, use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
module.trait.Pvalue <- corPvalueStudent(module.trait.correlation, n_trait)
# BH-FDR across modules
module.trait.FDR <- apply(module.trait.Pvalue, 2, p.adjust, method = "BH")
dimnames(module.trait.FDR) <- dimnames(module.trait.Pvalue)

# Supporting view: continuous TILs, Spearman (rank-based, so "<5" coded 2.5 does not matter)
okv <- !is.na(datTraits$TILs_value)
sp <- lapply(MEs, function(x) cor.test(x[okv], datTraits$TILs_value[okv],
                                       method = "spearman", exact = FALSE))
rho   <- unname(sapply(sp, function(z) unname(z$estimate)))
rho_p <- unname(sapply(sp, function(z) z$p.value))

assoc <- data.frame(
  Module = sub("^ME", "", colnames(MEs)),
  r_High_vs_Low   = unname(module.trait.correlation[, "TILs_High"]),
  P_High_vs_Low   = unname(module.trait.Pvalue[, "TILs_High"]),
  FDR_High_vs_Low = unname(module.trait.FDR[, "TILs_High"]),
  rho_TILs_continuous = rho,
  P_TILs_continuous   = rho_p,
  FDR_TILs_continuous = p.adjust(rho_p, method = "BH"),
  Module_size = as.integer(table(mergedColors)[sub("^ME", "", colnames(MEs))]),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
write.csv(assoc, file.path(wgcna_dir, "All_Module_TILs_Associations.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
print(assoc[order(assoc$P_High_vs_Low), ], digits = 3)
```

# 21. Module-TILs relationship heatmap

Each cell shows the correlation, with the BH-adjusted p-value (FDR) in brackets below it.
The FDR is calculated across modules, separately for each column.

```{r module-trait-heatmap}
heat_r <- cbind("TILs High vs Low" = assoc$r_High_vs_Low,
                "TILs continuous (Spearman)" = assoc$rho_TILs_continuous)
heat_p <- cbind(assoc$FDR_High_vs_Low, assoc$FDR_TILs_continuous)   # BH-FDR, not raw p
rownames(heat_r) <- colnames(MEs)
textMatrix <- matrix(paste0(signif(heat_r, 2), "\n(", signif(heat_p, 2), ")"),
                     nrow = nrow(heat_r))

plot_module_trait_heatmap <- function() {
  op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 1), oma = c(0, 0, 0, 0), mar = c(8, 12, 4, 3))
  on.exit(par(op))
  labeledHeatmap(
    Matrix = heat_r, xLabels = colnames(heat_r),
    yLabels = rownames(heat_r), ySymbols = rownames(heat_r),
    colorLabels = FALSE, colors = blueWhiteRed(50),
    textMatrix = textMatrix, cex.text = 0.6, cex.lab.x = 0.85, cex.lab.y = 0.70,
    zlim = c(-1, 1), main = "Module-TILs relationships (BH-FDR in brackets)"
  )
}
save_fig("Module_Trait_Relationships_TILs", plot_module_trait_heatmap,
           width_in = 7, height_in = max(7, 0.5 * nrow(heat_r) + 3))
```

# 22. Gene-level module membership (kME) and gene significance (GS)

kME is the correlation of a gene with its module eigengene (how central the gene is).
GS is the correlation of a gene with the TILs trait (High = 1, Low = 0).

```{r gene-level-kme-gs}
modNames <- substring(colnames(MEs), 3)   # drop the leading "ME"

geneModuleMembership <- as.data.frame(cor(dat_expr, MEs, use = "p"))
MMPvalue <- as.data.frame(corPvalueStudent(as.matrix(geneModuleMembership), nSamples))
colnames(geneModuleMembership) <- paste0("kME_", modNames)
colnames(MMPvalue) <- paste0("p.kME_", modNames)

geneTraitSignificance <- as.data.frame(cor(dat_expr, datTraitsNum, use = "p"))
GSPvalue <- as.data.frame(corPvalueStudent(as.matrix(geneTraitSignificance), n_trait))
colnames(geneTraitSignificance) <- paste0("GS_", colnames(datTraitsNum))
colnames(GSPvalue) <- paste0("p.GS_", colnames(datTraitsNum))

geneInfo <- data.frame(
  Gene = colnames(dat_expr),
  Module = unname(mergedColors),
  geneModuleMembership, MMPvalue, geneTraitSignificance, GSPvalue,
  check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL
)
# BH-FDR for gene significance across all genes
geneInfo$FDR_GS_TILs_High <- p.adjust(geneInfo[["p.GS_TILs_High"]], method = "BH")

write.csv(geneInfo, file.path(wgcna_dir, "WGCNA_GeneLevel_kME_GS.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
head(geneInfo[, 1:6])
```

# 23. Top positive and top negative module for TILs

* Positive module: highest positive correlation = higher in High-TILs tumours.
* Negative module: strongest negative correlation = higher in Low-TILs tumours.

No module names are supplied beforehand. The grey "module" (genes not assigned to any
module) is excluded. Modules are chosen by the size of the correlation, so check the FDR
column before interpreting a module: a top module with a large FDR is only the best of
weak candidates.

```{r identify-top-modules}
long <- data.frame(Module = assoc$Module, Trait = "TILs_High",
                   r = assoc$r_High_vs_Low, p = assoc$P_High_vs_Low,
                   FDR = assoc$FDR_High_vs_Low, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
candidates <- long[long$Module != "grey", ]

pick_module <- function(d, dir) {
  d <- if (dir == "pos") d[d$r > 0, ] else d[d$r < 0, ]
  if (nrow(d) == 0) return(NULL)
  d <- d[order(-abs(d$r)), ][1, ]
  d$direction <- dir
  d$Associated_with <- ifelse(dir == "pos", "High TILs", "Low TILs")
  d
}
top_pos <- pick_module(candidates, "pos")
top_neg <- pick_module(candidates, "neg")
selected_modules <- rbind(top_pos, top_neg)
stopifnot("No non-grey module available" = !is.null(selected_modules) && nrow(selected_modules) > 0)
rownames(selected_modules) <- NULL

print(selected_modules, digits = 3)
write.csv(selected_modules, file.path(wgcna_dir, "Selected_TILs_Associated_Modules.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)
```

# 24. Eigengene of the selected modules by TILs group

```{r selected-eigengene-plot, fig.width=8, fig.height=4.5}
plot_me_box <- function() {
  op <- par(mfrow = c(1, nrow(selected_modules)), mar = c(4.5, 4.5, 3.5, 1))
  on.exit(par(op))
  set.seed(SEED)
  g <- datTraits$TILs_group
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(selected_modules))) {
    mm <- selected_modules$Module[i]
    y <- MEs[, paste0("ME", mm)]
    boxplot(y[!is.na(g)] ~ g[!is.na(g)], outline = FALSE, las = 1, border = "grey40", col = NA,
            xlab = "TILs group", ylab = "Module eigengene",
            names = c(paste0("Low (<", TIL_CUTOFF, ")"), paste0("High (>=", TIL_CUTOFF, ")")),
            main = paste0(mm, " (", selected_modules$Associated_with[i], ")"))
    points(jitter(as.numeric(g), amount = 0.12), y, pch = 19, cex = 1.1,
           col = GROUP_COLORS[as.character(g)])
    mtext(sprintf("r = %.2f, FDR = %.3g", selected_modules$r[i], selected_modules$FDR[i]),
          side = 3, line = 0.3, cex = 0.8)
  }
}
save_fig("Selected_Module_Eigengene_by_TILs_Group", plot_me_box,
           width_in = 4 * nrow(selected_modules) + 1, height_in = 4.5)
```

# 26. Hub genes in each selected module

A gene is a hub gene if it differs between High and Low TILs (Wilcoxon rank-sum test,
BH-adjusted P < 0.05 within the module) and has module membership kME > 0.70. The effect
size is the mean VST difference (High minus Low), which is on a log2-like scale. Module
names come from the result above and are not hard-coded. With about 30 samples these
results are descriptive.

```{r identify-hub-genes}
stopifnot(identical(rownames(datTraits), rownames(dat_expr)))
grp   <- datTraits$TILs_group
ok_g  <- !is.na(grp)
all_hub_results <- list()

for (i in seq_len(nrow(selected_modules))) {
  module_name    <- selected_modules$Module[i]
  direction_name <- selected_modules$direction[i]

  module_genes <- colnames(dat_expr)[mergedColors == module_name]
  if (length(module_genes) == 0) {
    warning("No genes found for module ", module_name)
    next
  }

  y_mat <- dat_expr[ok_g, module_genes, drop = FALSE]
  g_ok  <- grp[ok_g]

  p_val <- apply(y_mat, 2, function(y) {
    tryCatch(wilcox.test(y[g_ok == "High"], y[g_ok == "Low"], exact = FALSE)$p.value,
             error = function(e) NA_real_)
  })
  mean_diff <- apply(y_mat, 2, function(y) mean(y[g_ok == "High"]) - mean(y[g_ok == "Low"]))

  kme_col <- paste0("kME_", module_name)
  stopifnot("Expected kME column not found" = kme_col %in% colnames(geneInfo))

  tab_m <- data.frame(gene = module_genes, p_value = as.numeric(p_val),
                      mean_diff_High_minus_Low = as.numeric(mean_diff),
                      stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  tab_m$adj_p <- p.adjust(tab_m$p_value, method = "BH")
  tab_m$kME   <- geneInfo[[kme_col]][match(tab_m$gene, geneInfo$Gene)]

  hub <- tab_m[!is.na(tab_m$p_value) & tab_m$adj_p < HUB_FDR_CUTOFF &
               tab_m$kME > HUB_KME_CUTOFF, , drop = FALSE]
  hub <- hub[order(-hub$kME, hub$p_value), , drop = FALSE]
  hub$trait     <- rep("TILs_High", nrow(hub))
  hub$direction <- rep(direction_name, nrow(hub))
  hub$module    <- rep(module_name, nrow(hub))
  hub <- hub[, c("trait", "direction", "module", "gene", "kME", "p_value", "adj_p",
                 "mean_diff_High_minus_Low")]

  write.csv(hub, file.path(wgcna_dir, paste0("HubGenes_TILs_High_", direction_name, "_",
                                             module_name, ".csv")), row.names = FALSE)
  cat("Module", module_name, "(", direction_name, "): genes =", length(module_genes),
      "| hub genes =", nrow(hub), "\n")
  all_hub_results[[paste(direction_name, module_name, sep = "_")]] <- hub
}

all_tils_hub_genes <- if (length(all_hub_results) > 0) do.call(rbind, all_hub_results) else data.frame()
rownames(all_tils_hub_genes) <- NULL
write.csv(all_tils_hub_genes, file.path(wgcna_dir, "All_TILs_HubGenes.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
cat("Total retained hub-gene rows:", nrow(all_tils_hub_genes), "\n")
head(all_tils_hub_genes)
```

# 27. Top 50 genes (by kME) for each selected module

```{r top50-hub-genes}
top50_list <- list()
for (i in seq_len(nrow(selected_modules))) {
  module_name    <- selected_modules$Module[i]
  direction_name <- selected_modules$direction[i]

  kme_col  <- paste0("kME_", module_name)
  pkme_col <- paste0("p.kME_", module_name)

  d <- geneInfo[geneInfo$Module == module_name, ]
  d <- head(d[order(-d[[kme_col]]), ], TOP_N)
  d <- d[, c("Gene", "Module", kme_col, pkme_col,
             "GS_TILs_High", "p.GS_TILs_High", "FDR_GS_TILs_High")]
  colnames(d)[3:4] <- c("kME", "p.kME")        # same names for every module
  d$Trait <- "TILs_High"
  d$Direction <- direction_name

  write.csv(d, file.path(wgcna_dir, paste0("Top50_Hub_Genes_TILs_High_", direction_name,
                                           "_", module_name, ".csv")), row.names = FALSE)
  top50_list[[paste("TILs_High", direction_name, module_name, sep = "_")]] <- d
}
top50_all_df <- do.call(rbind, top50_list)
write.csv(top50_all_df, file.path(wgcna_dir, "Top50_Hub_Genes_All_Selected_Modules.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)
```

# 29. Optional annotation of hub genes with the OncoVar/TCGA reference

```{r cancer-annotation}
annotated_core <- NULL

if (nrow(all_tils_hub_genes) == 0) {
  message("No hub genes passed the filters; cancer-gene annotation skipped.")
} else if (!file.exists(oncovar_file)) {
  message("OncoVar reference not found: ", oncovar_file,
          ". Cancer-gene annotation and annotated heatmaps skipped.")
} else {
  oncovar <- fread(oncovar_file, data.table = FALSE)
  stopifnot("OncoVar file has no Gene_symbol column" = "Gene_symbol" %in% colnames(oncovar))

  annotated_core <- all_tils_hub_genes[all_tils_hub_genes$gene %in% oncovar$Gene_symbol, ]
  rownames(annotated_core) <- NULL
  write.csv(annotated_core, file.path(wgcna_dir, "Annotated_Cancer_HubGenes.csv"),
            row.names = FALSE)
  cat("Cancer-associated hub-gene rows:", nrow(annotated_core), "\n")
}
```

# 30. Heatmaps for the annotated cancer-associated hub genes

```{r annotated-hubgene-heatmaps}
if (!is.null(annotated_core) && nrow(annotated_core) > 0) {
  for (dir_name in unique(annotated_core$direction)) {
    group_df <- annotated_core[annotated_core$direction == dir_name, ]
    genes <- intersect(unique(group_df$gene), colnames(dat_expr))
    assoc_with <- ifelse(dir_name == "pos", "High TILs", "Low TILs")
    cat(dir_name, ":", length(genes), "annotated genes available\n")

    ht <- make_tils_heatmap(genes, dat_expr, datTraits,
                            column_title = paste0("Annotated hub genes: ", assoc_with),
                            row_title = paste(length(genes), "genes"))
    if (is.null(ht)) {
      warning("Skipping heatmap for ", dir_name, ": fewer than 2 variable genes.")
      next
    }
    save_fig(paste0("AnnotatedHubGenes_TILs_High_", dir_name, "_Heatmap"),
               function() draw(ht), width_in = 11, height_in = 9)
  }
} else {
  message("No annotated hub genes; annotated heatmaps skipped.")
}
```
